    Home/Learn/Compounded vs brand semaglutide and tirzepatide

    Compounded or brand GLP-1: what you get, what it costs, what the FDA says.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 30 Oct 2026.

    Short answer

    Brand semaglutide (Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Zepbound) are FDA approved for weight management; compounded copies are not, and the FDA does not check them before they are sold.123

    What is compounding?

    Compounding means a pharmacist mixes a medicine for a patient on a prescription. It is meant for people an approved medicine does not suit, for example someone allergic to a dye in the tablet, or a child who needs a liquid.3

    Compounded medicines are not FDA approved. The FDA does not check their safety, how well they work or their quality before they are sold.3 Regular pharmacies (called 503A pharmacies, after the part of the law they work under) are mainly overseen by state boards; larger outsourcing facilities (503B) follow federal manufacturing rules and the FDA inspects them.3

    When may a pharmacy copy Wegovy or Zepbound?

    A pharmacy may make copies of a medicine that is on the FDA's drug shortages list, if it meets the conditions in federal law.3 That is how compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide came to be sold while both were in short supply.

    The FDA said the tirzepatide shortage was resolved in October 2024 and the semaglutide shortage in February 2025. It gave regular pharmacies until 22 April 2025 and outsourcing facilities until 22 May 2025 to stop making copies of semaglutide, and its page says neither medicine is on the shortage list.4

    Online clinics still sell compounded versions; our clinic table lists them next to the brand plans. The FDA also warns that some sellers use salt forms (semaglutide sodium or acetate), which are different ingredients from the one in the approved medicine, and that it knows of no lawful basis for using them.5

    What does the FDA say about compounded GLP-1s?

    The FDA has counted 990 reports of side effects linked to compounded semaglutide and more than 730 linked to compounded tirzepatide, as of 31 May 2026, and says the real numbers are likely higher because most pharmacies do not have to report them.5 It has also had reports of people taken to hospital after dosing mistakes with compounded semaglutide, where the dose was measured or worked out wrongly.5

    Compounded versions are often sent in vials that hold several doses, which you draw up yourself.5 We do not give doses; your prescriber does.

    What should you ask a clinic?

    • Is this the brand medicine (Wegovy, Zepbound) or a pharmacy-made copy?
    • Which pharmacy makes it, and is it a 503A pharmacy or a 503B outsourcing facility?
    • Is the price all-in, or is there a monthly care fee on top?
    • Does the price change when the dose goes up?
    • Has the clinic had an FDA warning letter? Our weight loss page shows the date of each clinic's newest one.

    None of this is medical advice. Your prescriber can tell you which medicine fits you.
